text: When the last espresso machine in the neighborhood cafe finally hissed its goodbye, the regulars reacted with something between grief and mild panic. For three decades, the corner shop on Linden Street had been a refuge for writers, freelancers, and the occasional philosopher. Its closure says something larger about what rising rents are doing to our communal third spaces. Talk to any barista who survived the pandemic and you will hear the same story: margins thinner than the crema on their flat whites.

Silicon Valley's latest obsession is not another chatbot, but the humble pickleball court. Executives who once filled their calendars with golf outings now schedule dawn doubles matches before boardroom battles. Some call it networking theater; others insist the sport's low barrier to entry makes it a genuine equalizer. Whatever the motive, the industry has already attracted venture capital, celebrity investors, and enough merch to outfit a small city. Whether the craze endures beyond a few summer seasons, however, remains anyone's guess.

It is tempting to dismiss the so-called slow reading movement as nostalgia dressed up in Scandinavian minimalism. But spend an afternoon at one of their monthly salons and you will find thoughtful people wrestling, genuinely, with ideas that do not fit in a tweet. The movement rejects skim culture without moralizing about it. That restraint, I think, is why it is catching on. In a year of shouting, a room full of people turning paper pages feels almost radical.

The northern lights came for Kansas this week, and nobody was prepared. Farmers stepping out to check their cattle reported skies of impossible green, streaked with pinks that rivaled any postcard from Tromso. Space weather forecasters had warned of a severe geomagnetic storm, yet the geographic reach still stunned observers. For a region that rarely makes astronomy headlines, it was a reminder that the sun keeps its own schedule, indifferent to ours.

Ask any veteran sportswriter what killed the beat reporter, and they will point first at the collapse of classified ads, then at social media, and finally at ownership groups who mistake cost cutting for strategy. What gets lost is the slow accumulation of knowledge: the sources cultivated over decades, the quiet interviews in empty clubhouses. A team's press release cannot replace that texture, even if the analytics dashboard pretends otherwise.

Reykjavik in November feels like a city holding its breath. The sun barely clears the harbor before retreating, and locals move through blue twilight with the quiet competence of people who have negotiated darkness their whole lives. Tourists expect gloom. What they find instead is a capital lit from within, its bookshops and swimming pools glowing like lanterns. You leave with the sense that the Icelanders have figured out something the rest of us missed.

The new wave of mid-budget films is quietly rescuing cinema from its blockbuster funk. Directors who spent a decade pitching to streamers are rediscovering the theatrical window, armed with budgets modest enough to take creative risks. Audiences, for their part, seem grateful for stories that do not involve multiverses or costumes that weigh more than the actors wearing them. Whether studios learn from the trend or suffocate it is an open question.

My grandmother kept a notebook of every loaf of bread she ever baked. Flour brand, hydration, weather, the mood of the kitchen. I found it last week, tucked behind a stack of seed catalogs, and spent an evening reading entries from 1974. The precision stunned me. She had been doing data science before anyone called it that, and her sourdough, I now understand, was the output of a forty-year experiment.

Downtown's newest gallery has no walls. Instead, the curator hangs paintings from suspended cables in a converted foundry, inviting visitors to weave between canvases as if walking through a forest. Critics are split: some call it gimmickry, others a genuine rethinking of how we encounter art. Attendance numbers, at least, do not lie. The opening drew lines around the block in a neighborhood that had not seen a queue for culture in years.

Electric vans are finally making sense for the people who actually need them. Ask a plumber doing six jobs a day across town, and the math now pencils out where it did not eighteen months ago. Fleet managers have noticed too, quietly swapping diesel workhorses for battery models that cost less to fuel and almost nothing to service. The revolution, as usual, is arriving through the service entrance rather than the showroom.

There is a particular kind of bookstore that cannot be replicated online, and Powell's is the archetype. Walk in on a rainy afternoon and you enter a warren of rooms where the categories bleed into each other and a clerk with ink-stained fingers will cheerfully argue that you are wrong about Bolano. Amazon sells more books. Powell's sells the afternoon.

The cycling boom of the early twenties left a peculiar legacy: a generation of adults who suddenly remember, viscerally, what freedom felt like at eleven. City planners have scrambled to catch up, paving protected lanes at a pace unthinkable a decade ago. Detractors grumble about parking. Proponents point to the children now riding to school unaccompanied, a small miracle many of us had written off as impossible in the age of the SUV.

There was a time when every small town had a mayor who could name half the residents on sight. That era is not quite dead, but it is wheezing. As hollowed-out downtowns give way to dollar stores and drive-thrus, the civic rituals that once stitched communities together have thinned. The question is whether the new crop of young candidates, many of them returning from big cities, can reweave what was lost.

I spent a week at a silent retreat in the Catskills and came home convinced my phone had been lying to me. Not about anything specific, just in the general sense that its endless notifications were passing themselves off as urgency when they were mostly noise. A friend asked me afterward whether the silence was boring. It was not. It was the first time in years my thoughts had room to finish themselves.

The farmer's market on Saturday mornings has become an unlikely political institution. Between the heirloom tomatoes and the sourdough stand, you can find petition tables, mayoral candidates pressing flesh, and retirees mapping out neighborhood watch routes. It is not the forum the founders imagined, but it may be the one we have. Democracy, like produce, is better when local.

Country music has always been a genre that claims to distrust change while quietly absorbing it. The latest crop of young artists out of East Nashville are the proof: pedal steel over trap drums, lyrics that quote both Townes Van Zandt and a group text. Purists hate it. Record labels cannot press vinyl fast enough. The tradition, as ever, survives by refusing to stand still.

Last winter's ice storm took out the power for six days, and my neighborhood learned something our grandparents knew: the grid is a promise, not a guarantee. By day three we were cooking communal meals over propane burners in the driveway. By day five, the teenagers had organized a library run for the elderly couple on the corner. The lights came back eventually. The street, for a while, did not need them.

We present a novel attention mechanism for long-context language models that reduces memory overhead by a factor of 4.2x without significant degradation in perplexity. Our method, termed sparse-banded attention, restricts the attention matrix to a block-diagonal structure learned jointly with the input embeddings. Experiments on the PG-19 and Long Range Arena benchmarks demonstrate parity with dense attention at context lengths up to 32,768 tokens. We release code and pretrained checkpoints to facilitate reproducibility.

Abstract. This study investigates the role of soil microbial diversity in mediating nitrogen retention under elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide. Using a randomized block design across twelve temperate grassland plots, we quantify shifts in bacterial and fungal community composition via 16S and ITS amplicon sequencing. Results indicate a statistically significant (p < 0.01) increase in nitrogen immobilization correlated with fungal-to-bacterial ratio. These findings refine existing biogeochemical models and suggest that microbial community structure is a non-negligible parameter in climate projections.

We propose a new estimator for causal effects under partial interference that relaxes the stable unit treatment value assumption (SUTVA). Theoretical analysis establishes consistency and asymptotic normality under mild regularity conditions. Monte Carlo simulations across 1,000 replications demonstrate lower mean squared error than standard inverse probability weighting, particularly in settings with clustered treatment assignment. We apply the method to a large-scale vaccine trial and report revised estimates of indirect protective effects.

This paper derives closed-form expressions for the equilibrium price in a continuous-time limit order book under the assumption of risk-neutral market makers with bounded inventory. The proposed model generalizes prior work by Almgren and Chriss to heterogeneous informed trading. We prove existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium via a fixed-point argument on the space of admissible strategies. Empirical calibration to high-frequency NASDAQ data yields parameter estimates consistent with theoretical predictions within a 95% confidence interval.

Abstract. We report the synthesis and characterization of a novel metal-organic framework (MOF-217) exhibiting selective carbon dioxide uptake at ambient temperature and pressure. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a previously unreported topology with pore diameters of 5.8 angstroms. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate a CO2/N2 selectivity of 142, surpassing benchmark materials Mg-MOF-74 and zeolite 13X. Density functional theory calculations rationalize the observed selectivity via favorable electrostatic interactions with open metal sites.

We investigate the convergence properties of stochastic gradient descent under heavy-tailed noise distributions. Prior analyses typically assume sub-Gaussian or bounded-variance gradients; we relax this assumption to the class of alpha-stable distributions with 1 < alpha <= 2. Under this setting, we establish an expected regret bound of O(T^((alpha-1)/alpha)) and demonstrate tightness via a matching lower bound. Empirical results on deep neural network training corroborate the theoretical scaling.

Abstract. This longitudinal cohort study (N = 4,872) examines the association between adolescent screen time and depressive symptomatology over a six-year follow-up period. Using cross-lagged panel models with fixed effects for individual heterogeneity, we find a small but statistically significant bidirectional relationship (standardized beta = 0.08, p < 0.001). Effect sizes do not support causal interpretations commonly advanced in the popular press. We discuss implications for clinical guidance and public health messaging.

We introduce a differentially private mechanism for federated learning that achieves (epsilon, delta)-privacy with improved utility relative to prior art. Our construction combines local Gaussian noise injection with a secure aggregation protocol, yielding a privacy amplification factor of sqrt(n) for n participating clients. Experiments on FEMNIST and Shakespeare benchmarks demonstrate accuracy within 1.3% of non-private baselines at epsilon = 1.0. We provide formal proofs and open-source implementations.

Abstract. We present a phylogenetic analysis of 312 complete mitochondrial genomes from extant and extinct Equidae, incorporating newly recovered ancient DNA from three Pleistocene specimens. Bayesian inference under a relaxed molecular clock places the divergence of modern horses and asses at approximately 4.7 million years before present (95% highest posterior density: 4.1-5.3 Mya). These results revise earlier estimates and have implications for our understanding of late Miocene grassland expansion.

This paper examines the welfare effects of minimum wage increases using a difference-in-differences design leveraging geographic variation in state-level policy between 2012 and 2022. Employing administrative payroll records covering 27 million workers, we estimate employment elasticities in the range of -0.08 to -0.15, with heterogeneity across industry and firm size. Our findings are robust to alternative control group specifications and to the synthetic control method of Abadie et al. (2010).

We describe a novel fault-tolerant quantum error correction scheme based on low-density parity-check codes on hyperbolic surfaces. The construction achieves a constant encoding rate of 1/12 and a threshold of approximately 0.7% under circuit-level depolarizing noise, as determined by Monte Carlo simulation of the belief propagation decoder. These results represent, to our knowledge, the first demonstration that hyperbolic LDPC codes outperform the surface code in the asymptotic regime.

Abstract. We conducted a double-blind, randomized controlled trial (N = 248) to evaluate the efficacy of a twelve-week mindfulness-based stress reduction program on cortisol awakening response in adults with chronic insomnia. The intervention group exhibited a 23% reduction in morning cortisol relative to active control (p = 0.003, Cohen's d = 0.42). Secondary outcomes included self-reported sleep quality and actigraphic measures. We discuss limitations and directions for future research.

This work presents a theoretical framework for analyzing the expressivity of graph neural networks beyond the Weisfeiler-Lehman hierarchy. We introduce a family of higher-order message-passing architectures parameterized by a locality radius k and prove a strict separation result: for every k there exists a graph distinguishable by our model but not by any k-WL-equivalent architecture. Experimental evaluation on molecular property prediction benchmarks confirms the theoretical advantage.

Abstract. Using high-resolution satellite imagery and convolutional neural networks, we produce the first continuous estimate of urban tree canopy cover across 102 African cities. Results indicate a median canopy cover of 8.3%, with substantial inter-city variation (interquartile range: 4.1%-14.7%). Canopy cover correlates negatively with population density (Spearman's rho = -0.51) and positively with per-capita income. We discuss implications for urban heat mitigation and climate adaptation policy.

We formalize and study the problem of online bipartite matching under adversarial vertex arrivals with predictions. Our main contribution is a learning-augmented algorithm achieving a competitive ratio of 1 - 1/e + Omega(eta), where eta characterizes prediction accuracy. The bound interpolates smoothly between the classical RANKING result and the optimal offline solution. We complement the upper bound with a matching lower bound up to lower-order terms.

Abstract. This paper reports results from a field experiment (N = 3,214 households) evaluating the impact of behavioral nudges on residential energy consumption. Treatment households received monthly social comparison reports benchmarking their usage against efficient neighbors. We observe an average reduction of 2.1% over the twelve-month study period (95% CI: 1.4%-2.8%), with persistent effects eighteen months after intervention cessation. Cost-effectiveness calculations suggest the program is competitive with traditional energy efficiency rebates.

We propose a unified variational framework for approximate Bayesian inference in state-space models with non-Gaussian observation noise. The method extends existing stochastic variational inference to handle heavy-tailed and discrete emissions via a reparameterized score-function estimator. Simulation studies demonstrate improved accuracy over particle filtering at comparable computational cost. We illustrate applicability on a neural spike train dataset and a financial volatility forecasting task.

In this tutorial you will set up a Python virtual environment and install the requests library. Step 1: Open your terminal and navigate to your project folder. Step 2: Run `python -m venv .venv` to create the environment. Step 3: Activate it with `source .venv/bin/activate` on macOS or Linux, or `.venv\Scripts\activate` on Windows. Step 4: Install the package by running `pip install requests`. Step 5: Verify the install with `python -c "import requests; print(requests.__version__)"`.

Let's build a simple REST endpoint with FastAPI. First, install the framework: `pip install fastapi uvicorn`. Next, create a file named `main.py` and add the following code: `from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()
@app.get('/')
def root(): return {'hello': 'world'}`. Now start the server with `uvicorn main:app --reload`. Finally, open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser. You should see the JSON response. In the next section we will add a POST route.

This guide walks you through baking a basic sourdough loaf. Step 1: Mix 500 g of bread flour, 350 g of water, and 100 g of active starter in a large bowl. Step 2: Let the dough rest for 30 minutes, then add 10 g of salt. Step 3: Perform four sets of stretch-and-folds, spaced 30 minutes apart. Step 4: Bulk ferment until the dough has risen by about 50%. Step 5: Shape, cold-proof overnight, then bake at 475F in a preheated Dutch oven for 25 minutes covered and 20 minutes uncovered.

To clone a Git repository and create your first branch, follow these steps. First, copy the repo URL from your provider. Then run `git clone <url>` in your terminal. Next, change into the new directory with `cd <repo-name>`. Now create a branch by running `git checkout -b feature/my-change`. Make your edits, stage them with `git add .`, and commit using `git commit -m "describe your change"`. Finally, push the branch to the remote with `git push -u origin feature/my-change`.

In this walkthrough you will deploy a static website to Netlify. Step 1: Sign in to Netlify and click "Add new site". Step 2: Connect your GitHub account and select the repository. Step 3: Set the build command to `npm run build` and the publish directory to `dist`. Step 4: Click "Deploy site" and wait for the build to complete. Step 5: Once the status turns green, visit the generated URL to confirm your site is live. To add a custom domain, proceed to the Domain settings panel.

Let's configure SSH key authentication for GitHub. First, generate a new key pair by running `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@example.com"`. Accept the default path and set a strong passphrase. Next, start the SSH agent with `eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"` and add the key using `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. Then copy the public key with `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` and paste it into GitHub under Settings > SSH keys. Finally, verify with `ssh -T git@github.com`.

This tutorial shows you how to make pour-over coffee. Step 1: Bring 400 g of water to 205F. Step 2: Weigh out 25 g of medium-coarse ground coffee into the filter. Step 3: Place the dripper on your carafe and rinse the filter with hot water, then discard. Step 4: Pour 50 g of water in a slow circle to bloom the grounds for 30 seconds. Step 5: Continue pouring in three pulses until you hit 400 g total. Step 6: Allow the drawdown to finish, then swirl and serve.

To create your first Docker container, follow these steps. First, install Docker Desktop from docker.com and verify with `docker --version`. Next, create a file named `Dockerfile` with the contents `FROM python:3.11-slim\nCMD ["python", "-c", "print('hello')"]`. Then build the image by running `docker build -t hello .` in the same directory. Finally, run the container with `docker run --rm hello`. You should see the greeting printed. Remove the image later with `docker rmi hello`.

In this section we will write your first unit test with pytest. Step 1: Install pytest by running `pip install pytest`. Step 2: Create a file named `test_math.py` and add the following: `def test_addition(): assert 1 + 1 == 2`. Step 3: Run the test suite with `pytest`. Step 4: Confirm you see `1 passed` in the output. Step 5: Add a failing test to see what errors look like, then correct it. You now have a working test harness to build on.

Let's set up a simple cron job on Linux to back up a folder nightly. First, open your crontab for editing with `crontab -e`. Next, add the following line: `0 2 * * * tar -czf /backup/home-$(date +\%F).tar.gz /home/user`. This runs every night at 2 AM. Save and exit the editor. Verify the job is installed by running `crontab -l`. Finally, check `/backup` the next morning to confirm the archive was created. Rotate or prune older archives with a second cron entry if needed.

To install Node.js using nvm, follow these steps. Step 1: Download the installer with `curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash`. Step 2: Close and reopen your terminal, or run `source ~/.bashrc`. Step 3: Confirm nvm is available by running `nvm --version`. Step 4: Install the latest LTS release with `nvm install --lts`. Step 5: Verify the Node version with `node --version`. You can switch versions later using `nvm use <version>`.

This guide teaches you to whip up homemade pesto. Step 1: In a food processor, combine two cups of fresh basil leaves, three cloves of garlic, and a quarter cup of pine nuts. Step 2: Pulse until coarsely chopped. Step 3: With the motor running, slowly drizzle in half a cup of olive oil. Step 4: Stop the processor and stir in half a cup of grated Parmesan cheese. Step 5: Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Toss immediately with warm pasta and serve.

Let's configure a PostgreSQL database for local development. First, install the server using your package manager, for example `brew install postgresql@16`. Next, start the service with `brew services start postgresql@16`. Then create a new database by running `createdb mydevdb`. Connect to it using `psql mydevdb` and create a test table with `CREATE TABLE items (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT);`. Exit the shell with `\q`. Finally, confirm persistence by reconnecting and running `\dt` to list your tables.

In this tutorial you will train a basic linear regression model with scikit-learn. Step 1: Install the library with `pip install scikit-learn`. Step 2: Import the model and load data: `from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression`. Step 3: Prepare your X and y arrays as NumPy arrays. Step 4: Instantiate the model with `model = LinearRegression()` and call `model.fit(X, y)`. Step 5: Make predictions using `model.predict(X_new)`. Step 6: Evaluate with `model.score(X_test, y_test)` to get the coefficient of determination.

To change a flat bicycle tire, follow these steps. First, flip the bike upside down and release the brakes. Then loosen the wheel's quick release and remove the wheel. Next, use tire levers to pry one edge of the tire off the rim. Pull out the old tube and inspect the inside of the tire for the cause of the puncture. Insert a new tube, seat both edges of the tire back onto the rim, and inflate to the pressure printed on the sidewall. Finally, remount the wheel and re-engage the brakes.

Let's create a simple React component from scratch. Step 1: Start a new project by running `npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react`. Step 2: Change into the directory with `cd my-app` and install dependencies using `npm install`. Step 3: Open `src/App.jsx` and replace its contents with `export default function App() { return

Hello

; }`. Step 4: Start the dev server with `npm run dev`. Step 5: Visit the printed URL to see your component render in the browser. Edit the file to see hot reload in action.

collections.deque(iterable=[], maxlen=None) returns a new deque object initialized left-to-right from iterable. Deques support thread-safe, memory-efficient appends and pops from either side with roughly O(1) performance. If maxlen is not specified, deques may grow to an arbitrary length; otherwise the deque is bounded, and new items added while the deque is full cause a corresponding number of items to be discarded from the opposite end. Key methods include append, appendleft, pop, popleft, extend, extendleft, rotate, and clear.

numpy.linalg.svd(a, full_matrices=True, compute_uv=True, hermitian=False) factors a matrix A into U, S, Vh such that A equals U @ diag(S) @ Vh. When full_matrices is True the returned U and Vh have shapes (M, M) and (N, N); when False they have shapes (M, K) and (K, N) where K equals min(M, N). The singular values S are always returned in descending order. Setting hermitian=True uses a faster eigenvalue decomposition path for Hermitian matrices.

torch.nn.LayerNorm(normalized_shape, eps=1e-5, elementwise_affine=True) applies Layer Normalization over a mini-batch. The mean and standard deviation are computed over the last D dimensions, where D is the length of normalized_shape. Unlike BatchNorm, statistics are computed per sample rather than across the batch, which makes LayerNorm suitable for sequence models and variable batch sizes. When elementwise_affine is True the module contains learnable per-element scale (gamma) and bias (beta) tensors with the same shape as normalized_shape.

Glossary term: Referential integrity. A database property that ensures relationships between tables remain consistent. Specifically, if a foreign key column references a primary key in a parent table, every non-null value in the foreign key must match an existing primary-key value. Referential integrity is typically enforced by FOREIGN KEY constraints, which may define ON DELETE and ON UPDATE actions such as CASCADE, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT, RESTRICT, or NO ACTION to control propagation of changes across related rows.

HTTP/1.1 status code 429 Too Many Requests indicates that the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time. Servers SHOULD include a Retry-After header field in the response, which can be either an HTTP-date or an integer number of seconds after which the client may retry. The 429 status is intentionally generic: servers are not required to reveal the rate-limiting policy, though many APIs return supplementary headers such as X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset to help clients self-regulate.

pandas.DataFrame.groupby(by=None, level=None, as_index=True, sort=True, dropna=True) groups a DataFrame using a mapper or by a series of columns. The returned GroupBy object supports aggregation via agg, transformation via transform, filtering via filter, and iteration over (group_key, sub_frame) pairs. When as_index is False, the grouped columns become regular columns in the result rather than the index. Passing dropna=False preserves NaN groups, which is useful for audit-style aggregations that must account for missing keys.

Rust trait std::iter::Iterator defines a method next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item>. Implementors must provide next; adapter methods such as map, filter, take, skip, chain, zip, and collect are supplied by default implementations. Iterators are lazy: no work is performed until a consuming method such as collect, count, sum, or for_each is called. Many adapters return their own Iterator types, enabling composition without heap allocation. The IntoIterator trait converts a type into an iterator and underpins Rust's for loop.

PostgreSQL function jsonb_path_query(target jsonb, path jsonpath [, vars jsonb [, silent bool]]) returns all JSON items produced by applying the given jsonpath expression to the target. The optional vars argument supplies named parameters referenced in the path as $name. When silent is true, errors raised during path evaluation are suppressed. For a single-result variant use jsonb_path_query_first, and for membership tests use jsonb_path_exists, which returns a boolean instead of expanding matches.

React hook useEffect(setup, dependencies?) runs the setup function after the component commits to the DOM. If setup returns a cleanup function, React calls it before the next setup run and again when the component unmounts. Dependencies control re-execution: passing an empty array runs setup only once after mount, passing a non-empty array runs setup whenever any referenced value changes by Object.is comparison, and omitting the argument runs setup after every render. Avoid object identity pitfalls by memoizing non-primitive dependencies.

Glossary term: Idempotent operation. An operation that produces the same result whether applied once or many times with the same input. In HTTP, the methods GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, and OPTIONS are defined as idempotent, while POST is not. Idempotency is a property of the effect on server state, not the response body. Clients use idempotency to safely retry requests after network failures; servers often support idempotency keys so that duplicate POST submissions are coalesced server-side.

Go package context provides Context values that carry deadlines, cancellation signals, and request-scoped values across API boundaries. context.Background returns an empty root Context, while context.TODO signals an unfinished design decision. Derived contexts are created by WithCancel, WithDeadline, WithTimeout, and WithValue. Callers must invoke the returned cancel function to release resources associated with the derived context, typically via defer. A Context becomes Done when any ancestor is cancelled or its deadline expires, and the Err method reports the cause.

Kubernetes resource HorizontalPodAutoscaler automatically scales the number of pods in a workload based on observed metrics. The spec fields minReplicas and maxReplicas bound the replica count; metrics list the signals used for scaling, such as Resource CPU utilization, Object metrics from a named resource, or External metrics from a metrics adapter. The behavior field under HPA v2 controls scale-up and scale-down policies, including stabilization windows that dampen rapid oscillations. The controller reconciles desired replicas every 15 seconds by default.

scikit-learn class sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler(copy=True, with_mean=True, with_std=True) standardizes features by removing the mean and scaling to unit variance. The fit method computes the mean and standard deviation per feature on the training set; transform applies the learned statistics. For sparse matrices, set with_mean=False to avoid densifying the data. The scaler exposes mean_, scale_, and var_ attributes after fitting. inverse_transform recovers the original scale, which is useful when predictions must be returned in the original feature units.

Glossary term: Two-phase commit (2PC). A distributed-transaction protocol coordinating commit across multiple resource managers. In the prepare phase, the coordinator asks each participant to durably record intent to commit and reply prepared or abort. If all reply prepared, the coordinator writes a commit record and sends commit messages; otherwise it sends abort. 2PC guarantees atomicity under the assumption of durable logs and eventually reachable participants, but it blocks indefinitely if the coordinator fails after some participants have acknowledged prepare.

Linux system call epoll_ctl(int epfd, int op, int fd, struct epoll_event *event) modifies the set of file descriptors monitored by an epoll instance. The op argument is EPOLL_CTL_ADD, EPOLL_CTL_MOD, or EPOLL_CTL_DEL. The events field of struct epoll_event is a bitmask including EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLRDHUP, EPOLLPRI, EPOLLERR, EPOLLHUP, EPOLLET for edge-triggered mode, and EPOLLONESHOT. The data field is an opaque user token returned by epoll_wait when the descriptor becomes ready.

TypeScript utility type Partial<T> constructs a type with all properties of T set to optional. It is implemented as { [P in keyof T]?: T[P] }. Related helpers include Required<T>, which strips optionality, Readonly<T>, which makes properties read-only, and Pick<T, K>, which selects a subset of keys. These mapped types compose with conditional types such as Exclude<T, U> and Extract<T, U> to express richer transformations, enabling API authors to derive patch, view, and update types from a single source of truth.

Redis command ZADD key [NX | XX] [GT | LT] [CH] [INCR] score member [score member ...] adds members with scores to the sorted set stored at key. NX only adds new elements; XX only updates existing ones; GT updates a score only if the new one is greater; LT only if lesser. CH changes the reply to the number of elements added or updated rather than just added. INCR, valid for a single score-member pair, increments the score instead of replacing it and returns the new score.

BRUSSELS, April 14 — European Union lawmakers approved a revised package of clean-industry subsidies on Monday, giving member states expanded authority to match state aid offered by competitors in the United States and China. The measure, backed by a 412-163 vote in the European Parliament, covers battery plants, green hydrogen, and grid-scale storage. Commission Vice-President Maros Sefcovic told reporters the package would unlock an estimated 180 billion euros of investment by 2030. Environmental groups criticized the deal for loosening limits on fossil-based hydrogen.

SAN FRANCISCO — A federal appeals court on Tuesday reinstated a class-action lawsuit against a major rideshare platform, ruling that drivers may pursue claims they were misclassified as independent contractors. The three-judge panel of the Ninth Circuit reversed a lower-court order compelling arbitration, citing a 2024 state statute that exempts gig-economy disputes from mandatory arbitration clauses. The plaintiffs, represented by the worker advocacy group Rideshare United, said the ruling could affect more than 300,000 drivers statewide. The company said it would appeal.

TOKYO, April 15 — The Bank of Japan held its benchmark short-term rate at 0.5 percent on Thursday, citing softening wage growth and uneven household spending. Governor Kazuo Ueda told a post-meeting news conference that the central bank would wait for more data before considering a further move. The yen weakened to 156.30 against the dollar after the announcement. Analysts at Nomura said they now expect the next rate decision to come in July rather than June, as markets had priced in earlier this month.

NAIROBI — Kenya's Ministry of Health reported on Friday that a cholera outbreak in the coastal county of Kilifi has grown to 1,240 confirmed cases and 22 deaths since early March. Health Cabinet Secretary Susan Nakhumicha said mobile treatment units had been deployed in three affected sub-counties and that the World Health Organization was supplying oral rehydration salts. Officials traced the outbreak to contaminated boreholes damaged during recent floods. A vaccination campaign targeting 250,000 residents is expected to begin next week, the ministry added.

LONDON — Shares in British engineering firm Rolls-Royce rose 4.8 percent on Wednesday after the company raised its full-year profit forecast, citing stronger aftermarket demand for its civil aerospace engines. Chief Executive Tufan Erginbilgic told investors the Trent XWB fleet had flown 14 percent more hours in the first quarter than a year earlier. The FTSE 100 component now expects underlying operating profit of between 2.7 and 2.9 billion pounds for 2026, up from a prior range of 2.5 to 2.7 billion. Competitors Safran and Pratt & Whitney also gained.

WASHINGTON — The Federal Trade Commission sued a leading grocery-delivery platform on Monday, accusing it of using dark patterns to enroll customers in an auto-renewing membership and making cancellation unreasonably difficult. The complaint, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, seeks civil penalties and refunds for affected consumers. FTC Chair Lina Khan said the case reflected the agency's broader push against subscription traps. The company denied wrongdoing and said it would vigorously defend its signup and cancellation flows in court.

SEOUL, April 12 — South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor announced Saturday it will invest 4.6 trillion won, about 3.4 billion dollars, in a new electric-vehicle plant in Ulsan that is scheduled to begin production in late 2028. The facility will have annual capacity of 200,000 vehicles and will produce the company's next-generation SUV platform. Labor union officials welcomed the decision after weeks of uncertainty about domestic manufacturing commitments. Trade Minister Ahn Duk-geun said the project would create roughly 2,500 direct jobs in the southeastern industrial region.

OTTAWA — Canada's statistics agency said inflation eased to 2.4 percent year-over-year in March, down from 2.7 percent in February, bringing the rate closer to the Bank of Canada's 2 percent target. Shelter costs remained the largest contributor, rising 5.1 percent, while gasoline prices fell 3.8 percent. Economists polled by Reuters had expected 2.5 percent. Governor Tiff Macklem reiterated last week that rate decisions would remain data-dependent. Markets now price a roughly 60 percent probability of a 25-basis-point cut at the Bank's June meeting.

CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Launch Complex 40 at 3:17 a.m. local time Thursday, carrying 22 Starlink satellites into low Earth orbit. The first-stage booster, making its 19th flight, landed on the droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas in the Atlantic eight minutes after liftoff. Thursday's mission brought the operational Starlink constellation above 6,800 active satellites. Company President Gwynne Shotwell said a follow-up launch from Vandenberg Space Force Base is scheduled for Saturday.

GENEVA — The World Trade Organization on Friday downgraded its forecast for global merchandise-trade growth in 2026 to 2.1 percent from an earlier projection of 3.0 percent, citing heightened tariff uncertainty and weaker demand in Europe. Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala told a briefing the downgrade underscored the need for renewed multilateral cooperation. The report singled out a deceleration in semiconductor and automotive shipments. Trade between North America and Asia nonetheless continued to expand, partially offsetting softer European activity, WTO economists said in the accompanying outlook.

JAKARTA — Indonesia's parliament passed a long-debated personal data protection amendment on Wednesday, imposing fines of up to 2 percent of annual global turnover on companies that mishandle citizens' data. The bill also creates a new supervisory authority under the Ministry of Communication and Informatics. Minister Budi Arie Setiadi said enforcement would begin in January 2027 after a nine-month transition. Industry group APJII cautiously welcomed the framework but warned that small businesses would need technical guidance to comply with the breach-notification rules.

MEXICO CITY — Mexican oil company Pemex reported a first-quarter net loss of 43.7 billion pesos on Tuesday, narrower than the 79.9-billion-peso loss a year earlier, as higher crude prices offset declining output. Production averaged 1.76 million barrels per day, down 2.4 percent year-over-year. Chief Executive Octavio Romero told reporters the company was on track to meet its 1.8-million-barrel target by year-end. Finance Minister Rogelio Ramirez de la O reiterated that the federal government would continue supporting Pemex with targeted capital injections.

BERLIN — Germany's Federal Cartel Office on Monday opened an investigation into a leading food-delivery aggregator over concerns about restrictive clauses imposed on partner restaurants. Authority President Andreas Mundt said the probe would examine whether most-favored-nation clauses prevent restaurants from offering lower prices on their own websites. The company said it would cooperate fully and believed its practices complied with German and EU competition law. A preliminary decision is expected within nine months, the regulator said in its statement.

SYDNEY — Australian researchers reported Thursday that the Great Barrier Reef is experiencing its most severe bleaching event on record, with aerial surveys showing bleaching across 73 percent of the 1,200 reefs assessed. Dr. Neal Cantin of the Australian Institute of Marine Science said sustained sea-surface temperatures more than 2 degrees Celsius above the March average were the primary driver. Environment Minister Tanya Plibersek pledged an additional 150 million Australian dollars for reef-resilience programs. Recovery will depend on whether cooler autumn temperatures arrive within three weeks.

ATHENS — Greek firefighters battled a wildfire on the island of Rhodes for a third day on Sunday, with gusts of up to 80 kilometers per hour hampering containment efforts. Civil Protection Minister Vassilis Kikilias said 420 firefighters, 12 aircraft, and 4 helicopters were deployed; approximately 1,300 residents and tourists were evacuated from three villages. No fatalities have been reported. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis declared a state of emergency for the southern part of the island and requested assistance under the EU Civil Protection Mechanism.

NEW DELHI — India's Election Commission announced Friday that phase four of the general election will be held on April 29, covering 96 parliamentary constituencies across 10 states. Chief Election Commissioner Rajiv Kumar said more than 177 million voters would be eligible to cast ballots at 101,000 polling stations. Security forces from 11 states will be redeployed to ensure peaceful voting. Final results for the seven-phase nationwide vote are scheduled to be released on June 4 alongside counts from the earlier phases.

STOCKHOLM — Ericsson reported a 15 percent drop in first-quarter sales on Tuesday, citing continued weakness in North American 5G investments. Net sales fell to 53.3 billion Swedish crowns, broadly matching analyst expectations, while adjusted operating margin improved to 9.5 percent thanks to cost cuts announced last year. Chief Executive Borje Ekholm said demand would stabilize in the second half as operators began planning 5G Advanced rollouts. Shares fell 2 percent in early Stockholm trading before partially recovering in afternoon sessions.

Classic Tomato Bruschetta. Ingredients: 4 ripe Roma tomatoes diced, 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, 6 fresh basil leaves chiffonade, 1 garlic clove minced, half a teaspoon kosher salt, a quarter teaspoon black pepper, 1 baguette sliced 1.5 centimeters thick. Steps: 1. Combine tomatoes, basil, garlic, oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl; let rest 15 minutes. 2. Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat, brush bread with oil, and toast 90 seconds per side. 3. Spoon tomato mixture onto warm toasts and serve immediately.

Weeknight Miso Soup. Ingredients: 4 cups dashi stock, 3 tablespoons white miso paste, 150 grams soft silken tofu cubed, 2 tablespoons dried wakame, 2 scallions sliced thin. Steps: 1. Rehydrate wakame in cold water 5 minutes, then drain. 2. Bring dashi to a gentle simmer, about 85 degrees Celsius; do not boil. 3. Whisk miso with a ladle of warm dashi in a small bowl until smooth, then stir back into the pot. 4. Add tofu and wakame, warm 2 minutes, top with scallions, and serve.

Lemon-Garlic Roast Chicken. Ingredients: 1 whole chicken about 1.6 kilograms, 1 lemon halved, 6 garlic cloves smashed, 3 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon kosher salt, 2 teaspoons black pepper, 4 thyme sprigs. Steps: 1. Preheat oven to 220 degrees Celsius. 2. Pat the chicken dry, rub with oil, salt, and pepper, and stuff cavity with lemon, garlic, and thyme. 3. Roast breast-up on a rack for 55 to 65 minutes until a thigh thermometer reads 74 degrees Celsius. 4. Rest 10 minutes before carving.

Chickpea Curry (Chana Masala). Ingredients: 2 cans chickpeas drained, 1 large onion diced, 3 garlic cloves minced, a 2-centimeter piece of ginger grated, 1 can diced tomatoes, 2 teaspoons garam masala, 1 teaspoon cumin, half a teaspoon turmeric, 3 tablespoons vegetable oil, salt to taste. Steps: 1. Heat oil in a deep pan, saute onion until golden, about 8 minutes. 2. Add garlic, ginger, and spices; cook 1 minute until fragrant. 3. Stir in tomatoes and chickpeas; simmer uncovered 20 minutes until thickened. 4. Season and serve with rice.

Buttermilk Pancakes. Ingredients: 250 grams all-purpose flour, 2 tablespoons sugar, 1 teaspoon baking powder, half a teaspoon baking soda, half a teaspoon salt, 480 milliliters buttermilk, 2 large eggs, 60 grams melted butter. Steps: 1. Whisk dry ingredients together. 2. In a second bowl whisk buttermilk, eggs, and butter. 3. Fold wet into dry until just combined; small lumps are fine. 4. Rest batter 10 minutes. 5. Cook quarter-cup portions on a 180-degree-Celsius griddle until bubbles pop and edges set, about 2 minutes, then flip and finish 1 minute.

Garlic Shrimp Linguine. Ingredients: 350 grams linguine, 450 grams peeled shrimp, 4 garlic cloves sliced, a quarter teaspoon red pepper flakes, 120 milliliters dry white wine, 3 tablespoons butter, 3 tablespoons olive oil, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 2 tablespoons chopped parsley. Steps: 1. Boil pasta in salted water until al dente, reserving a cup of cooking water. 2. Saute garlic and chili in oil 1 minute. 3. Add shrimp, cook 2 minutes per side. 4. Pour wine, reduce 1 minute, swirl in butter, toss with pasta and lemon, and serve.

Overnight Oats. Ingredients: 80 grams rolled oats, 200 milliliters milk, 60 grams Greek yogurt, 1 tablespoon chia seeds, 2 teaspoons maple syrup, a quarter teaspoon vanilla extract, 80 grams mixed berries. Steps: 1. In a 350-milliliter jar, combine oats, milk, yogurt, chia, maple syrup, and vanilla; stir well. 2. Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours or up to 48 hours. 3. Stir before serving to loosen; top with berries. For a thicker texture use an additional teaspoon of chia. Keeps in the refrigerator up to three days.

Beef Stew. Ingredients: 900 grams beef chuck cut into 4-centimeter cubes, 3 tablespoons flour, 3 tablespoons oil, 1 large onion diced, 3 carrots sliced, 2 celery ribs sliced, 3 garlic cloves, 240 milliliters red wine, 720 milliliters beef stock, 2 tablespoons tomato paste, 2 bay leaves, salt and pepper. Steps: 1. Toss beef with flour and brown in oil in batches. 2. Saute aromatics 5 minutes. 3. Deglaze with wine, scraping the fond. 4. Add stock, tomato paste, and bay; simmer covered at 160 degrees Celsius for 2 hours until fork-tender.

No-Knead Bread. Ingredients: 400 grams bread flour, 8 grams fine sea salt, 2 grams instant yeast, 320 milliliters lukewarm water. Steps: 1. Mix flour, salt, yeast, and water with a spatula until a shaggy dough forms. 2. Cover and let rise at room temperature 12 to 18 hours. 3. Turn onto a floured surface, shape into a round, and proof 90 minutes on parchment. 4. Preheat a Dutch oven to 245 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes. 5. Bake covered 30 minutes, uncover and bake 15 more minutes until deep golden.

Thai Green Curry. Ingredients: 3 tablespoons green curry paste, 400 milliliters coconut milk, 500 grams chicken thigh sliced, 1 Thai eggplant cubed, 100 grams bamboo shoots, 1 tablespoon fish sauce, 2 teaspoons palm sugar, 6 Thai basil leaves, 2 kaffir lime leaves. Steps: 1. Fry paste in 3 tablespoons of thick coconut cream over medium heat 2 minutes until aromatic. 2. Add chicken; stir 3 minutes. 3. Pour remaining coconut milk, bring to a gentle simmer. 4. Add vegetables; cook 10 minutes. 5. Season with fish sauce, sugar, and basil; serve with jasmine rice.

Caesar Salad. Ingredients: 1 romaine heart chopped, 60 grams parmesan shaved, 80 grams croutons. Dressing: 2 anchovy fillets, 1 garlic clove, 1 egg yolk, 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 teaspoon Worcestershire, 120 milliliters neutral oil, salt and pepper. Steps: 1. Mash anchovies and garlic into a paste. 2. Whisk in yolk, mustard, lemon juice, and Worcestershire. 3. Drizzle oil in slowly while whisking to emulsify. 4. Toss romaine with dressing, season, and top with parmesan and croutons just before serving.

Chocolate Chip Cookies. Ingredients: 225 grams butter softened, 200 grams light brown sugar, 100 grams granulated sugar, 2 large eggs, 2 teaspoons vanilla, 320 grams all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1 teaspoon salt, 300 grams chocolate chips. Steps: 1. Cream butter and sugars 3 minutes until fluffy. 2. Beat in eggs and vanilla. 3. Mix in flour, soda, and salt until just combined, then fold in chips. 4. Chill dough 30 minutes. 5. Scoop 45-gram balls onto lined trays and bake at 190 degrees Celsius for 11 minutes until edges set.

Greek Tzatziki. Ingredients: 300 grams thick Greek yogurt, half an English cucumber grated, 2 garlic cloves grated, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 2 teaspoons chopped dill, half a teaspoon salt. Steps: 1. Squeeze cucumber firmly in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as possible, yielding roughly 80 grams of flesh. 2. Combine all ingredients in a bowl and stir well. 3. Cover and chill at least 1 hour so the garlic mellows. 4. Taste and adjust salt and lemon before serving with warm pita or grilled meats.

Shakshuka. Ingredients: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 onion diced, 1 red pepper diced, 3 garlic cloves minced, 2 teaspoons smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 can (400 grams) crushed tomatoes, 4 large eggs, 60 grams feta crumbled, 2 tablespoons chopped parsley. Steps: 1. Heat oil in a 25-centimeter skillet, saute onion and pepper 8 minutes. 2. Add garlic and spices; cook 1 minute. 3. Pour tomatoes, simmer 10 minutes until thickened. 4. Make 4 wells, crack an egg into each, cover, and cook 6 minutes until whites set. 5. Top with feta and parsley.

Banana Bread. Ingredients: 3 very ripe bananas mashed, 115 grams melted butter, 150 grams brown sugar, 2 large eggs, 1 teaspoon vanilla, 220 grams flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, half a teaspoon salt, 80 grams chopped walnuts. Steps: 1. Preheat oven to 175 degrees Celsius and grease a 23-by-13-centimeter loaf pan. 2. Whisk bananas, butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla. 3. Fold in flour, soda, and salt until just combined; stir in walnuts. 4. Pour into pan and bake 55 to 65 minutes until a skewer emerges clean. 5. Cool 15 minutes before slicing.

Vietnamese Pickled Carrots and Daikon (Do Chua). Ingredients: 250 grams carrots julienned, 250 grams daikon julienned, 1 tablespoon salt, 180 milliliters rice vinegar, 180 milliliters warm water, 100 grams sugar. Steps: 1. Toss carrot and daikon with salt; let sit 15 minutes, then squeeze gently and rinse. 2. Whisk vinegar, water, and sugar until the sugar dissolves. 3. Pack vegetables into a 750-milliliter jar and pour brine to cover. 4. Refrigerate at least 1 hour before use; flavor peaks at 48 hours and keeps up to 3 weeks.

-- Top 10 customers by revenue over the trailing 30 days, excluding internal test accounts.
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.display_name,
       SUM(o.total_cents) / 100.0 AS revenue_usd,
       COUNT(*)                    AS order_count
FROM   orders       AS o
JOIN   customers    AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE  o.placed_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
  AND  o.status = 'fulfilled'
  AND  c.is_internal = FALSE
GROUP  BY c.customer_id, c.display_name
ORDER  BY revenue_usd DESC
LIMIT  10;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rotate local log files older than 14 days into a dated tarball and remove the originals.
set -euo pipefail

LOG_DIR="${1:-/var/log/myapp}"
ARCHIVE_DIR="${LOG_DIR}/archive"
mkdir -p "$ARCHIVE_DIR"

cd "$LOG_DIR"
mapfile -t OLD < <(find . -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.log' -mtime +14)
if [[ ${#OLD[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "nothing to rotate"
  exit 0
fi

STAMP=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
tar -czf "${ARCHIVE_DIR}/logs-${STAMP}.tar.gz" "${OLD[@]}"
rm -f "${OLD[@]}"

import httpx
import asyncio

async def fetch_all(urls: list[str], concurrency: int = 8) -> list[bytes]:
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
        async def one(url: str) -> bytes:
            async with sem:
                resp = await client.get(url)
                resp.raise_for_status()
                return resp.content
        return await asyncio.gather(*(one(u) for u in urls))

1.  Introduction.  This document specifies the wire format for the Darkmem Memory Transport Protocol, Version 2 (MTP/2).  Implementations MUST accept frames of at most 65,535 octets and SHALL reject frames whose declared length exceeds the octets actually received.  Frames MAY be fragmented across TCP segments; receivers SHALL reassemble using the sequence number in octets 4 through 7.  The keywords MUST, SHOULD, and MAY in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14.

2.  Frame Header.  Each MTP/2 frame begins with a fixed eight-octet header.  Octet 0 carries the version nibble in the high four bits and flags in the low four bits.  Octets 1 and 2 encode the payload length in network byte order.  Octet 3 is reserved and SHALL be transmitted as zero and ignored on receipt.  Octets 4 through 7 carry the monotonically increasing sequence number.

3.  Handshake.  On connection establishment the initiator SHALL send a HELLO frame whose payload is the ASCII literal "MTP/2" followed by a single space and the decimal capability bitmap.  The responder MUST reply within two seconds with a HELLO-ACK or else the initiator SHALL close the connection.  Capability bits undefined in this specification SHALL be set to zero and MUST be echoed unchanged by the responder.

4.  Keep-Alive.  A peer that has not transmitted a data frame for thirty seconds SHALL emit a PING frame carrying an opaque eight-octet token.  The remote peer MUST answer with a PONG frame echoing the same token within five seconds.  After two consecutive missed PONGs the local peer SHALL consider the session dead and MUST tear the connection down without transmitting further data frames.

5.  Error Codes.  Error frames carry a two-octet code in network byte order.  Codes 0x0001 through 0x00FF are reserved for transport errors and MUST be emitted only by the transport layer.  Codes 0x0100 through 0x0FFF are reserved for application errors.  Codes 0x1000 and above are experimental and SHALL NOT be used on the public Internet without prior IANA registration.

6.  Flow Control.  Each direction of an MTP/2 session maintains an independent credit window initialised to 65,536 octets.  A sender SHALL NOT transmit data frames whose cumulative payload exceeds the remaining credit.  Receivers MUST replenish credit by emitting WINDOW frames; a WINDOW frame carrying a zero increment is reserved for future use and SHALL be treated as a protocol error by current implementations.

7.  Compression.  Implementations MAY negotiate payload compression during the handshake by setting bit 3 of the capability bitmap.  When compression is active each data frame payload SHALL be a single DEFLATE stream terminated by its end-of-block marker.  Receivers MUST refuse frames larger than the negotiated maximum uncompressed size and SHALL report the condition with error code 0x0007.

8.  Authentication.  Mutual authentication SHALL be performed over TLS 1.3 using certificates issued by a trust anchor configured out of band.  Clients MUST present a certificate whose Subject Alternative Name matches the configured service identifier.  Servers MUST reject connections whose client certificate has been revoked according to the Online Certificate Status Protocol response cached no more than four hours prior.

9.  Session Resumption.  A peer MAY offer a resumption ticket of at most 128 octets in a RESUME frame sent immediately after HELLO-ACK.  Resumption tickets SHALL be opaque to the peer and MUST be bound cryptographically to the issuing session so that replay across sessions is detectable.  Implementations SHOULD expire tickets after twenty-four hours regardless of declared validity.

10.  Graceful Shutdown.  A peer that wishes to close a session cleanly SHALL transmit a BYE frame and then cease transmitting data frames.  The remote peer MUST drain outstanding data frames, acknowledge the BYE within one second, and then close the underlying TCP connection.  Implementations SHALL NOT send a RST-style close before both BYE frames have been exchanged except in response to a protocol violation.

11.  Identifier Format.  Memory identifiers exchanged over MTP/2 SHALL be sixteen-octet RFC 4122 version 7 UUIDs.  Endpoints MUST reject any identifier whose version nibble is not 0x7 and SHALL emit error code 0x0021.  Textual representations of identifiers outside the wire format SHOULD use the canonical hyphenated form and MUST preserve lowercase hexadecimal digits.

12.  Extensibility.  Future revisions of this specification MAY introduce new frame types by consuming currently reserved values of the type octet.  Implementations that encounter an unknown frame type SHALL respond with error code 0x0003 and MUST NOT attempt to process the payload.  A peer that receives three consecutive unknown-type errors SHOULD treat the session as incompatible and tear it down.

13.  Character Encoding.  Textual fields in control frames SHALL be encoded in UTF-8 without a byte order mark.  Receivers MUST reject frames that contain ill-formed UTF-8 sequences with error code 0x0009 and SHALL NOT attempt substitution of replacement characters.  Implementations SHOULD normalise identifiers to Unicode Normalization Form C prior to comparison but MUST NOT alter stored text.

14.  Time Values.  Timestamps transmitted in MTP/2 SHALL be 64-bit signed integers expressing microseconds since the Unix epoch.  Implementations MUST treat negative values as an error and SHALL report error code 0x0011.  Clock skew tolerance SHOULD be no greater than sixty seconds; peers that detect larger skew SHOULD emit a warning frame but MUST NOT terminate the session on that basis alone.

15.  Security Considerations.  This specification does not itself provide confidentiality; implementations SHALL run MTP/2 exclusively over TLS 1.3 or a successor mandated by IETF consensus.  Operators MUST NOT expose MTP/2 endpoints on unencrypted transports even within trusted networks.  Implementations SHOULD rate-limit handshake attempts from any single peer to no more than ten per minute.

16.  IANA Considerations.  This document requests IANA to register the TCP port 4712 as "mtp2" with the service name "Darkmem Memory Transport".  IANA SHALL also maintain the MTP/2 Frame Type registry with an initial allocation policy of "Specification Required".  Requests for values in the experimental range 0xF0 through 0xFF MAY be granted on a first-come-first-served basis.

17.  Backward Compatibility.  Implementations of MTP/2 MUST NOT interoperate with MTP/1 on the same TCP port because their handshake frames are indistinguishable in the first octet.  Operators who must support both versions SHALL expose MTP/1 on a separate port.  Future revisions SHALL introduce a version-negotiation octet so that single-port operation becomes feasible without ambiguity.
